ACME Ops: hey @Alex @support, our client #acme-prod p99 jumped from ~180ms to 3.5s around 2024-11-02T13:02:10Z. All requests from eu-west1 are showing a hop to us-west1 in traces. Users seeing timeouts and some 502s. trace id: trace-0a1b2c3d. link: https://acme-traces.example/trace-0a1b2c3d
Alex: sorry cc'ing @Jamal, looking now. can you paste the raw trace hops?
ACME Ops: here's the top of the span list, pasted from our tracer: 
```
client -> edge-eu1 (13.02.10.123)
edge-eu1 -> transit-eu (13.02.10.130)
transit-eu -> us-west-egress (13.02.10.145)
us-west-egress -> model-host-usw (13.02.10.350)
```
Also a sample request log: `POST /v1/generate 200 3500ms`
DeployBot: auto-failover: tenant=acme-prod action=route_to_fallback_region fallback_region=us-west1 reason=node_unhealthy detected_at=2024-11-02T13:03:05Z
Jamal: can you share the request-id / trace-id headers and a curl that reproduces? also any tenant config that might influence routing?
ACME Ops: request-id header `req-9f8e7d`. We can repro with this curl: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <redacted>" -H "X-Req-ID: req-9f8e7d" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' -v`
Lina: looking at egress telemetry — I see an abrupt drop in advertised eu egress prefixes at ~13:02Z, traffic for the eu NAT pool shifted to upstream that prefers an us-west path. BGP looked normal before flap, now investigating peer Hessian.
Maria: was this tenant pinned to a model variant in eu? could fallback be selecting a different model in us-west?
Alex: tenant config shows `prefer_local: true` and `fallback_regions: [us-west1]` with `fallback_priority: 2`. It should only fallback if eu pool is unhealthy. config snippet: 
```
{"tenant":"acme-prod","prefer_local":true,"fallback_regions":[{"region":"us-west1","priority":2}],"unhealthy_threshold":3}
```
Jamal: metrics show proxy tcp_rtt p50->p99 delta at 13:02: p50 120ms -> 160ms, p99 340ms -> 3.1s. Also increased retransmits from edge-eu1 to transit-eu. attaching small metric extract: `edge_eu1.tcp_retransmits: 0->18`
ACME Ops: we have a pcap we can share via secure link if needed. impact is real: some customers timed out and retried which amplified load.
Alex: I've temporarily applied a per-tenant policy to prefer_nearest_region=true and disabled cross-region failover for acme-prod while we root cause (rolling back the failover policy). Can you confirm if latency improves on your end?
ACME Ops: confirmed — p99 dropped to ~130ms within 90s. Good. fewer 502s. thanks.
Alex: initial conclusion: an egress peering flap (upstream) caused eu egress NAT addresses to be announced on a path that preferred us-west egress; our health checks saw elevated errors and marked eu pool partially unhealthy which triggered the fallback to us-west. That produced cross-region hops and 3s+ p99.
Alex: next steps: 1) SRE to open incident PRD-512 with full timeline and BGP adjacency logs, 2) Network to follow up with peering provider and request stability SLA adjustment, 3) Product/Platform to add per-tenant egress-stickiness option and alert on sudden egress-nat pool shifts, 4) consider relaxing unhealthy_threshold for automatic cross-region failover to reduce flapping.
Jamal: creating incident PRD-512 now and scheduling postmortem. adding links to traces/pcap in the incident.
Maria: will track product follow-up for egress-stickiness feature.
ACME Ops: appreciate the quick mitigation. we'll hold for postmortem and include our pcap.
Lina: locking down forensics: saving BGP dumps, egress-nat allocation logs, and control-plane health-check traces. will add to PRD-512.
DeployBot: changelog: tenant-policy-update acme-prod changed prefer_nearest_region=true at 2024-11-02T13:05:17Z by Alex
Alex: closing loop here — latency normalized after mitigation. We'll keep the tenant override until postmortem actions are implemented. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
